## Social Forms & Embodiment
Three essays by Toby Shorin and one Vulture profile form a cohesive cluster around embodied practice, social forms, and the shift away from software-centric utopianism.
- [[2026-03-25-body-futurism]] — the shift from software utopianism to body futurism: kinesthetic media, health protocols, protocolism, and the Human Potential movement's return
- [[2026-03-25-theory-of-social-forms]] — defining social forms as structured arrangements of people, distinct from institutions; pattern languages + play theory; cultural renewal through prototyping new forms
- [[2026-03-25-forms-of-life-centers]] — philosophical art exhibition on Centers (healing spaces); Neoplatonism, Christopher Alexander, form as design method, magic and social forms
- [[2026-03-25-will-wright-proxi-mind-game]] — Will Wright's decade-long quest to build Proxi, a game simulating the player's mind and memories; cognitive modeling as game design

## Open Questions
- The Toby Shorin cluster (body futurism + social forms + centers) represents a coherent intellectual thread about post-institutional organizing. Does the user have a take on this, or is this still in collection mode?
- Body futurism discusses the same "institutional decomposition → new forms" thesis as Venkatesh Rao's liveness work — but from an embodied/phenomenological angle rather than a systems/engineering one. Bridge?
- Will Wright's Proxi touches on cognitive modeling and simulation — connects to the AI agents thread through a completely different door (game design as agent architecture)

## Connections to Other Domains
- **AI Agents & Tools** — Claude's Constitution piece lives in both domains; PostHog's agent harness evolution is pure tech but its governance implications connect here
- **Business, Strategy & AI Economics** — Shorin's social forms theory explicitly contrasts with institutional theory (North's definition); the governance assertion thread overlaps via institutional decomposition
- **Governance assertion** — body futurism's "protocolism" (technical protocols → body protocols) directly parallels the governance talk's concern with how governance patterns migrate across domains
